question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 18 hours, pipe B can fill the same tank in 21 hours and pipe C can fill the same tank in 16 hours. The time taken by them to fill the same tank if they operate together is::
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total Capacity of tank = LCM(18, 21, 16) = 1008 units.

Combined Efficiency = (1008 ÷ 18) + (1008 ÷ 21) + (1008 ÷ 16) = 56 + 48 + 63 = 167 units/hr.

Time to fill together = Total Capacity ÷ Combined Efficiency = 1008 ÷ 167 = 6 ⁶/₁₆₇ hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 ⁶/₁₆₇ hours.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe A = 18 hours

Time taken by Pipe B = 21 hours

Time taken by Pipe C = 16 hours

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of given time periods

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time Taken

Time Taken Together = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

 **Hours**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total combined efficiency = 56 + 48 + 63 = 167 units/hr

⇒ Time taken to fill the tank together = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 1008 ÷ 167 = 6 ⁶/₁₆₇ hours

**∴ The correct answer is 6 ⁶/₁₆₇ hours.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns Concept

If a pipe can fill a tank in x hours, the part of the tank filled in 1 hour is 1/x. This unit-work approach is equivalent to finding fractional efficiency.

Inlet vs Outlet Pipes

Inlet pipes add water to the tank, so their efficiency is taken as positive. Outlet (leak) pipes remove water, so their efficiency is taken as negative when computing combined net work.

Efficiency & Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time taken (Efficiency = Work ÷ Time). A pipe that takes fewer hours to fill a tank has a higher individual filling capacity.
